generation.final_prompt:
Rendering style:
Create an authored editorial illustration for a serious technology newspaper.

Direction:
- authored editorial print language
- deliberate simplified shapes with clear focal hierarchy
- restrained limited palette
- subtle physical print texture
- controlled abstraction and strong negative space
- non-photorealistic but factually grounded representation
- newspaper and social-card readability

Fixed factual and safety restrictions:
- Do not render visible text, captions, headlines, or newspaper typography.
- Do not render logos or trademarks.
- Do not fabricate visible factual evidence.
- Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
- Do not imitate a named or living artist.

Profile-specific exclusions:
- glossy CGI
- luxury product render
- generic futuristic concept art
- cyberpunk or neon
- glowing circuit-board decoration
- floating particles
- heroic centered hardware
- server rack treated as monument or skyscraper
- generic server room
- advertising composition
- airbrushed gradients
- synthetic chrome
- excessive pseudo-technical detail
- malformed or visible text
- labels
- diagrams with words

Exact source facts:
Title: ANTHROPIC JOINS THE AI AGENT RACE WITH CLAUDE DUET
Summary: Anthropic's Claude Duet joins a fast-growing field of AI assistants that take actions and perform tasks on their own. Unlike OpenAI's dots and Meta's Muse, Anthropic's agent was built for work and is less capable at personal errands. It can connect to more than 6,000 outside apps and make purchases through Link, Stripe's digital wallet, and Shopify's Shop Pay. The agent shows users exactly what it plans to do before performing actions, and some actions, like trading stocks or moving money between accounts, are blocked even with user approval. The wait list to use the agent is now open to Anthropic's Pro and Max plan subscribers.

Editorial idea:
An autonomous work assistant expands its reach across connected services while approval gates and blocked actions define the boundary of user control.

Central subject:
Claude Duet acting across connected work applications

Visual relationship:
The agent's ability to perform tasks across more than 6,000 apps is balanced against explicit user approval and restrictions on financial actions.

Composition:
A person stands at the center of a large office desk while folders and objects from different work areas are linked by a single assistant's set of hands; a clear physical boundary at the desk edge separates actions the assistant may prepare from actions that remain with the person.

Permitted literal elements:
a person reviewing an assistant's proposed action
multiple distinct work documents and service interfaces represented without logos or rendered text
a visible boundary between proposed tasks and restricted financial actions
the assistant handling routine connected tasks while the person retains final control

Abstraction level:
medium

Story-specific forbidden elements:
racks
chips
laptops
robots
clouds
shields
arrows
charts
skyscrapers
chess
handshakes
split-screen conflict
logos
rendered text

Likely failure modes to avoid:
depicting the assistant as fully independent without approval gates
showing unsupported physical devices or app interfaces
turning the concept into a generic humanoid robot
using isolated software symbols instead of showing delegated work and retained control

Global factual restrictions:
Do not fabricate visible factual evidence. Do not imitate a named or living artist. Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
Do not render any words, letters, numbers, labels, captions, annotations, signage, diagrams with text, logos, watermarks, or pseudo-writing anywhere in the image.
If the concept cannot be represented without visible text, represent the relationship through shape, scale, spacing, direction, grouping, interruption, containment, or contrast instead.
